head:
USDT in.
Compute out.
post:
AIST P2P is live.

One book: BTC, USDT on five networks, KGST, ETH, SOL — and fiat. Bank transfer, card, mobile wallet, cash.

Escrow on every trade. No SWIFT, no listing queue.

assetux.com

head:
8 ways to trade
the spread
post:
We wrote the guide we wanted when we started.

8 P2P strategies, each with the steps, a worked example in real numbers, and the risk that actually costs money.

assetux.com/strategies

head:
Withdraw your
compute earnings
post:
Your GPU takes AI jobs and gets paid in compute coins.

This is where those coins turn into something your bank, your wallet or your landlord accepts.

assetux.com

head:
Simple spread
arbitrage
post:
The same pair, the same minute, two makers who disagree on price.

On a thin P2P book the best ask and best bid cross more often than they should — makers leave quotes up and walk away.

assetux.com/strategies#spread

head:
Payment method
arbitrage
post:
The same USDT is worth different money depending on how the money moves.

Cash is cheap to buy with. Instant bank transfer is expensive. The gap between them is the trade.

assetux.com/strategies#payment

head:
Cross-exchange
arbitrage
post:
KGST trades on Binance and on our book at the same time.

Two venues, two order books, one asset — and no rule that says they must agree.

Hold balance on both. Chasing the gap means arriving after it closes.

assetux.com/strategies#cross

head:
Geographic
arbitrage
post:
Stablecoins cost more where the local currency is under pressure.

Bishkek, Tbilisi and Addis do not price USDT the same way on the same Tuesday.

assetux.com/strategies#geo

head:
P2P market
making
post:
Stop hunting for a spread and quote one instead.

You post both sides, wait, and get paid by whoever is in a hurry. You are not calling direction — you are selling immediacy.

assetux.com/strategies#mm

head:
Inventory and
volatility
post:
Holding a payout for four days instead of selling it Monday is a position, whether you call it one or not.

This is the only strategy in the guide that can lose your principal rather than your spread.

assetux.com/strategies#inventory

head:
P2P liquidity
providing
post:
Market making on one pair, industrialised.

Commit a float across several assets and payment methods, and treat the fills as yield on capital.

assetux.com/strategies#liquidity

head:
Triangular
arbitrage
post:
Three pairs whose prices imply a fourth that does not exist.

Walk the loop. If the implied rate disagrees with the real one, you come back with more than you left with.

assetux.com/strategies#triangular

head:
Price the
round trip
post:
A 1.4% spread looks like money until you price the whole loop.

Two on-chain fees and one bank charge can take it under zero on small size.

The spread is not the profit. The round trip is.

assetux.com/strategies

head:
Escrow runs
15 minutes
post:
If a leg cannot finish inside the escrow window, it is not one trade.

It is two positions.

Size and plan accordingly.

assetux.com/strategies

head:
Depth beats
price
post:
The best quote for 200 KGST tells you nothing about where 200,000 KGST actually fills.

Everyone screenshots the top of book. The fill happens somewhere else.

assetux.com/strategies

head:
Keep float on
both sides
post:
An opportunity you have to fund first is usually gone by the time the funding lands.

Capital in the wrong place is the same as no capital.

assetux.com/strategies

head:
Adverse
selection
post:
In a one-way market only your losing side gets hit.

You buy all the way down and never sell.

Widen or pull the quote when the mid stops oscillating and starts trending.

assetux.com/strategies#mm

head:
Idle float is
the real cost
post:
Escrow ties capital up while an order is live.

A book full of your quotes can look busy while most of your money earns nothing.

Measure return on the whole float, not on the fill.

assetux.com/strategies#liquidity

head:
Leg three is
the thin one
post:
Compute-coin books are shallow.

The rate you multiplied by is often not the rate you get — and the position you are left holding is the hardest one to exit.

Most paper triangles die on leg three.

assetux.com/strategies#triangular

head:
USDT on
five networks
post:
Pick the network at the ticket, not at the pair.

TRC20 for cheap settlement. ERC20 when the counterparty insists. BEP20, TON or SOL when the fee matters more than the habit.

assetux.com

head: Bitcoin
post:
Deepest liquidity of any quote on the book.

The maker posts a receiving address, you send from any wallet, and escrow holds the base side until it lands.

assetux.com

head: KGST
post:
Already listed on Binance, so its price is not ours to invent.

Every compute coin quotes against it — which is exactly what makes the triangle trades work.

assetux.com

head: Fiat methods
post:
Bank transfer, card-to-card, mobile wallet, cash in person.

The maker names the method and the window. Escrow only releases once you confirm the money landed.

assetux.com

head: ETH and SOL
post:
Native ETH straight out of MetaMask — the UI builds the transaction, you sign it.

Connect Phantom on Solana to autofill your receive address. Sub-cent fees make small, frequent arbitrage legs viable.

assetux.com

head:
Cash out weekly,
not eventually
post:
No minimum payout. No listing queue. No SWIFT.

A miner earning 4,000 KGST a week cashes out weekly instead of waiting for a threshold that never quite arrives.

assetux.com

head:
Three steps from
GPU to bank
post:
Run the jobs — your node settles AI compute work in KGST or a regional compute coin.

List the payout on the P2P book at your own price.

Take it out in USDT, BTC, ETH, SOL or fiat.

assetux.com

head: Minimum payout
post:
Zero.

No threshold to reach, no queue to join, no wire to explain to a compliance desk.

You earned it, you list it, you take it out.

assetux.com

head:
What your node
really pays you
post:
KGST is the rail. aiGEL, aiETB and aiBTN are the regional compute coins.

Nothing to claim, nothing to unstake — finished work settles straight into the asset.

assetux.com

head:
Be the book,
not the taker
post:
Every taker who wants out right now pays someone for the privilege.

Provide the float that lets them, and that payment is your yield — earned on inventory you were holding anyway.

assetux.com/strategies#liquidity

head:
Where the edge
actually is
post:
Thin pairs pay the widest edge and fill slowly.

KGST-USDT pays the least and fills constantly.

Split your float across methods and let the fills come to you.

assetux.com/strategies#liquidity

head:
You never front
a stranger
post:
The base side locks the moment an order is selected, and stays locked for 15 minutes.

Making a market on a P2P book does not mean extending credit on good faith.
